# Default context pack — the framework's canonical numbered tree.
# This is the layout every starter vault ships with, so a workspace with no pack of its own
# uses the seven-group marketing template. Existing vaults migrate or declare legacy paths.
# Copy it with `init_context_pack.py` to author a pack for a
# workspace whose folders are named differently; never edit this file to describe one customer.
pack: default
schema: 1
title: Framework default layout
summary: Numbered vault tree — 10-ME, 20-COMPANY, 30-CLIENTS, 40-RESOURCES, 50-PROJECTS

roots:
  workspace: .
  me: 10-ME
  company: 20-COMPANY
  clients: 30-CLIENTS
  resources: 40-RESOURCES
  projects: 50-PROJECTS
  core: 00-CORE
  skills: 00-CORE/Agents/skills
  schemas: 00-CORE/Schemas
  templates: 00-CORE/Templates
  tasks: 00-CORE/TaskNotes/Tasks
  scratch: 99-TMP/OUTPUT
  tmp: 99-TMP

# Logical keys. `{id}` is the client, project, lead or partner identifier; keys without `{id}`
# resolve without one. A trailing `/` marks a folder. `summary` says what an agent will find
# there so it can decide whether to open it. `required: true` means validation fails when the
# path is absent on disk, and `template:` names the file under the templates folder a scaffold
# seeds it from. `scaffold: false` marks a folder the pack describes but a fresh workspace is not
# given empty — an evidence folder its first run creates reads as a department when it ships.
keys:
  me.profile:
    path: 10-ME/00-PROFILE/profile.md
    template: context/profile_personal.md
    required: true
    summary: Owner identity, role, working preferences
  me.root:
    path: 10-ME/
    summary: The owner's personal root folder
  me.constitution:
    path: 10-ME/00-PROFILE/constitution.md
    summary: Owner values and trade-offs, written by personal-context-builder
  me.comms:
    path: 10-ME/03-COMMS/
    summary: Personal communication threads — messages that belong to no client or company file
  me.people:
    path: 10-ME/10-PEOPLE/
    summary: Person notes for contacts that belong to no client
  me.meetings:
    path: 10-ME/20-MEETINGS/
    summary: Personal meetings with no company or client in the room
  me.ideas:
    path: 10-ME/30-IDEAS/
    summary: Unshaped ideas and what-if scripts
  me.decisions:
    path: 10-ME/02-DECISIONS/
    scaffold: false  # created by the first personal decision
    summary: The owner's personal decisions with no company or client scope — the same type decision record as company.decisions; check before re-deciding
  me.inbox:
    path: 10-ME/90-INBOX/
    summary: Unfiled captures, briefly
  me.playbooks:
    path: 10-ME/Playbooks/
    summary: Personal executable procedures
  me.personas:
    path: 10-ME/00-PROFILE/personas/
    summary: The owner's personal personas — the audience the owner writes as or for, separate from the company's buyer personas

  company.profile:
    path: 20-COMPANY/00-PROFILE/profile.md
    template: context/profile_company.md
    required: true
    summary: Legal identity, entity_id, jurisdiction, finance calendar — read before any company, finance or jurisdiction-sensitive routing
  company.root:
    path: 20-COMPANY/
    summary: The company root folder itself — every company-owned area sits under it
  company.clients:
    path: 30-CLIENTS/
    summary: The clients root — one folder per client relationship; use client.root with an id for one client
  company.projects:
    path: 50-PROJECTS/
    summary: The internal projects root — one folder per project; use project.root with an id for one project
  company.icp:
    path: 20-COMPANY/00-PROFILE/icp.md
    summary: Ideal customer profile — the canonical buyer
  company.offerings:
    path: 20-COMPANY/00-PROFILE/offerings.md
    summary: Services and products sold, with pricing posture
  company.marketing-context:
    path: 20-COMPANY/00-PROFILE/marketing_context.md
    summary: Positioning, messaging, competitive landscape, customer language
  company.brand:
    path: 20-COMPANY/00-PROFILE/brand/
    scaffold: false  # created by the brand skills when the company has a brand spec
    summary: Brand spec, colours, logo assets
  company.personas:
    path: 20-COMPANY/00-PROFILE/personas/
    summary: Buyer personas
  company.decisions:
    path: 20-COMPANY/02-DECISIONS/
    summary: Closed decisions, including the ones that closed "no" — check before recommending
  company.processes:
    path: 20-COMPANY/03-PROCESSES/
    summary: Process definitions and policies
  company.process-definitions:
    path: 20-COMPANY/03-PROCESSES/definitions/
    summary: The process library — one folder per defined process, holding its definition and policies
  company.process-audits:
    path: 20-COMPANY/03-PROCESSES/audits/
    summary: Process audit records — findings, waste observations and the AI initiatives raised from them
  company.processes.playbooks:
    path: 20-COMPANY/03-PROCESSES/Playbooks/
    summary: Playbooks that belong to a documented process rather than to the canonical playbook library
  company.runs:
    path: 20-COMPANY/03-PROCESSES/runs/
    summary: Run evidence for company operations — traces, patch logs, audit notes
  company.schedule-runs:
    path: 20-COMPANY/03-PROCESSES/schedule-runs/
    summary: Scheduled-job evidence — raw run logs under logs/, distilled metrics, crontab backups
  company.legal:
    path: 20-COMPANY/04-LEGAL/
    summary: Contracts and templates
  company.legal.contracts:
    path: 20-COMPANY/04-LEGAL/CONTRACTS/
    scaffold: false  # created when the first signed agreement is filed
    summary: Signed agreements the company is party to, insurance policies included — one note per contract
  company.legal.retention:
    path: 20-COMPANY/04-LEGAL/RETENTION/
    scaffold: false  # created when a retention schedule is first written
    summary: Document-retention schedules — what must be kept, for how long, and under which rule
  company.legal.freezone:
    path: 20-COMPANY/04-LEGAL/FREEZONE/
    scaffold: false  # only a free-zone registered entity has these
    summary: Free-zone licence and status records for the company's registered entities
  company.hr:
    path: 20-COMPANY/05-HR/
    summary: People operations — the company layer of people files (framework, values, cycle dates, role templates); names no individual
  company.performance-framework:
    path: 20-COMPANY/05-HR/performance-framework.md
    scaffold: false  # written by performance-framework's render route when a business adopts the framework
    summary: The company's layered performance framework instance — compliance gates, six universal dimensions with level anchors and evidence types, role-family modules, industry overlay, scale, cadences, version and valid-from
  company.hr.recruiting:
    path: 20-COMPANY/05-HR/recruiting/
    scaffold: false  # created by the first open role
    summary: Candidates and the sourcing channels they came through, for the company's own open roles
  company.hr.wps:
    path: 20-COMPANY/05-HR/WPS/
    scaffold: false  # only a jurisdiction with a wage protection system has these
    summary: Wage Protection System filings — the salary transfer records a labour authority requires
  company.hr.employees:
    path: 20-COMPANY/05-HR/EMPLOYEES/
    summary: One note per person employed after hire — role, start date, pay band, contract reference; the record `person` and `candidate` leave open
  company.hr.payroll:
    path: 20-COMPANY/05-HR/PAYROLL/
    summary: Payroll runs — one per pay period, carrying the per-person amounts the filings are built from
  company.hr.timesheets:
    path: 20-COMPANY/05-HR/TIMESHEETS/
    summary: Hours worked per person per period, split across the clients and projects they were worked on
  company.finance:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/
    summary: The books — ledger, invoices, bank, tax
  company.finance.ledger:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/BEANCOUNT/ledger/
    scaffold: false  # created by the beancount setup, which also writes its files
    summary: The company's plain-text accounting ledger files
  company.finance.expenses:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/AP/EXPENSES/
    summary: Employee expense claims and the receipts backing them — the accounts-payable side of spend someone paid for personally
  company.finance.ap:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/AP/
    summary: Accounts payable — what the company owes, from requisition through purchase order to the supplier invoice that settles it
  company.finance.ap-invoices:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/AP/INVOICES/
    summary: Invoices suppliers have sent the company, one note per invoice — the payable side of the ledger
  company.finance.ap-orders:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/AP/ORDERS/
    summary: Purchase orders the company has issued — what was committed to a supplier before the invoice arrives
  company.finance.ap-requisitions:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/AP/REQUISITIONS/
    summary: Internal purchase requests awaiting approval — the step before a purchase order exists
  company.finance.bank:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/BANK/
    summary: Bank accounts and their reconciliations — the statement side the ledger is agreed against
  company.finance.tax:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/TAX/
    summary: Tax filings and positions — corporate tax, VAT, deferred tax and transfer pricing each sit one level down
  company.finance.tax-ct:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/TAX/CT/
    summary: Corporate tax returns and the computations behind them, one per tax period
  company.finance.tax-vat:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/TAX/VAT/
    summary: VAT returns and the workings for each filing period
  company.finance.tax-deferred:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/TAX/DEFERRED/
    summary: Deferred tax computations — temporary differences and the balances they carry forward
  company.finance.tax-tp:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/TAX/TP/
    summary: Transfer pricing documentation for related-party transactions
  company.finance.assets-fixed:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/ASSETS/FIXED/
    summary: The fixed-asset register — one note per asset with cost, depreciation, impairment and disposal
  company.finance.assets-leases:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/ASSETS/LEASES/
    summary: Leases as accounted for — right-of-use assets and the liability schedule behind each one
  company.finance.periods:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/PERIODS/
    summary: Accounting periods and whether each is open or closed — read before posting anything dated
  company.finance.close:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/CLOSE/
    scaffold: false  # written by the first period close, not shipped empty
    summary: Period-close checklists and the evidence each close produced
  company.finance.journals:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/JOURNALS/
    summary: Manual journal entries posted outside the ledger's own automation
  company.finance.coa:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/COA/
    summary: Charts of accounts, one per jurisdiction the company keeps books in
  company.finance.reports:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/REPORTS/
    summary: Financial statements, their notes and the trial balances they are built from
  company.finance.provisions:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/PROVISIONS/
    scaffold: false  # written when a provision is first recognised
    summary: Provisions recognised against future obligations, with the basis each was measured on
  company.finance.provisions-gratuity:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/PROVISIONS/GRATUITY/
    scaffold: false  # written by the first end-of-service computation
    summary: End-of-service gratuity provisions per employee under the applicable labour law
  company.finance.inventory:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/INVENTORY/
    scaffold: false  # opened only by a company that carries stock
    summary: Inventory counts and valuations — quantities on hand and what they are carried at
  company.finance.fx:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/FX/
    summary: Foreign-exchange rate tables the books translate with, one per period and source
  company.finance.ecl:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/ECL/
    scaffold: false  # evidence folder, written by the first expected-credit-loss assessment
    summary: Expected-credit-loss assessments on receivables — the IFRS 9 impairment working
  company.finance.audit:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/AUDIT/
    scaffold: false  # opened when an external audit is actually engaged
    summary: External audit engagements — scope, the auditor's requests and the responses given
  company.finance.payment-cards:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/PAYMENT-CARDS/
    scaffold: false  # written when the first card is registered
    summary: Company payment cards, their holders and limits — the spend channel behind card transactions
  company.finance.ai-ledger:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/AI-LEDGER/
    scaffold: false  # evidence folder, written by the first ai-session-ledger run
    summary: AI session cost log, one note per day and client — the basis for recharging AI spend
  company.finance.entity:
    path: 20-COMPANY/06-FINANCE/ENTITY.md
    scaffold: false  # written by the bookkeeping setup, not shipped with the workspace
    summary: The company's books profile — reporting currency, fiscal calendar and the accounting policies its own ledger is kept under
  company.knowledge-base:
    path: 20-COMPANY/07-KNOWLEDGE-BASE/
    summary: Methodology the company owns and reuses across engagements
  company.people:
    path: 20-COMPANY/10-PEOPLE/
    summary: Restricted per-person layer — one folder per staff member holding goals, 1:1 notes, reviews, development plans and compliance-gate records; never placed in a shared or released folder
  company.meetings:
    path: 20-COMPANY/20-MEETINGS/
    summary: Internal meetings — no client in the room
  company.suppliers:
    path: 20-COMPANY/30-SUPPLIERS/
    summary: Someone the company pays
  company.partners:
    path: 20-COMPANY/35-PARTNERS/
    summary: Someone who resells or co-delivers
  company.products:
    path: 20-COMPANY/40-PRODUCTS/
    summary: Product definitions, pricing tiers, release configs
  company.products.installations:
    path: 20-COMPANY/40-PRODUCTS/installations/
    summary: Deployed installations of the company's products — one note per customer install and its version
  company.marketing:
    path: 20-COMPANY/50-MARKETING/
    summary: The company's own content and channels
  company.marketing.channels:
    path: 20-COMPANY/50-MARKETING/03-CHANNELS/accounts/
    summary: The company's own social channels — handle, audience and posting cadence per channel
  company.marketing.email:
    path: 20-COMPANY/50-MARKETING/03-CHANNELS/email/
    summary: Email sequences the company sends on its own behalf, separate from the sales pipeline's outbound
  company.marketing.geo-runs:
    path: 20-COMPANY/50-MARKETING/07-INSIGHTS/GEO/prompt-panel/runs/
    scaffold: false  # evidence folder, written by the first prompt-panel run
    summary: Generative-engine visibility probe runs — one folder per run, one per platform inside it
  company.marketing.skool-courseware:
    path: 20-COMPANY/50-MARKETING/03-CHANNELS/skool/courseware/
    summary: Skool course material — one folder per course, holding its modules and lessons
  company.marketing.skool-tracker:
    path: 20-COMPANY/50-MARKETING/03-CHANNELS/skool/tracker/
    summary: Weekly Skool community metrics — one note per week
  company.marketing.youtube:
    path: 20-COMPANY/50-MARKETING/05-PRODUCTION/video/youtube/
    summary: The company's own YouTube videos — scripts, metadata and publishing state per video
  company.leads:
    path: 20-COMPANY/55-LEADS/
    summary: Prospects that are not yet clients — one folder per lead
  company.sales:
    path: 20-COMPANY/60-SALES/
    summary: Pipeline mechanics — proposals, campaigns, never the won relationship
  company.sales.proposals:
    path: 20-COMPANY/60-SALES/PROPOSALS/
    summary: Proposals and quotes in flight — the pipeline artefact, not the won client's copy
  company.sales.price-lists:
    path: 20-COMPANY/60-SALES/PRICE-LISTS/
    summary: Versioned standard, partner and internal pricing a quote or timesheet cites by version; a client's negotiated rate card lives in that client's own sales folder
  company.sales.campaigns:
    path: 20-COMPANY/60-SALES/CAMPAIGNS/
    summary: Outbound campaigns — target list, offer and results per campaign
  company.sales.sequences:
    path: 20-COMPANY/60-SALES/SEQUENCES/
    summary: Outbound message sequences the campaigns send, one note per sequence
  company.operations:
    path: 20-COMPANY/70-OPERATIONS/
    summary: Systems and support
  company.operations.surveys:
    path: 20-COMPANY/70-OPERATIONS/SURVEYS/
    summary: Surveys the company runs and the responses they gathered
  company.management:
    path: 20-COMPANY/80-MANAGEMENT/
    summary: Management reporting, KPI registry, current state, strategy
  company.strategy:
    path: 20-COMPANY/80-MANAGEMENT/STRATEGY/
    summary: Company-wide strategy documents — the whole business, not one division; a division's own strategy is division.strategy
  company.decision-journal:
    path: 00-CORE/Bases/Decisions.base
    summary: The decision log, read as the Decisions Base over the per-decision records in company.decisions, client.decisions and me.decisions; the single-note decision_journal.md is retired (superseded) and no longer written
  company.project-management:
    path: 20-COMPANY/80-MANAGEMENT/projects/
    summary: Company project-management artifacts — registers, decisions and change logs; the company twin of client.project-management
  company.rocks:
    path: 20-COMPANY/80-MANAGEMENT/rocks/
    scaffold: false  # written by the first quarterly planning session
    summary: Quarterly rocks, one folder per quarter — the small number of outcomes that quarter commits to
  company.weather-forecast:
    path: 20-COMPANY/WEATHER-FORECAST/
    scaffold: false  # demo entity for the weather-forecast skill, not a department
    summary: Weather forecast notes written by the weather-forecast demo skill
  company.reports:

  company.kpi-reports:

  company.risks:
    path: 20-COMPANY/80-MANAGEMENT/RISKS/
    summary: The business risk register — forward-looking risks across the whole business, separate from the process-scoped QMS findings and issues

    path: 20-COMPANY/90-INBOX/
    summary: Unfiled company captures

  client.hr:

  client.hr.employees:

    summary: Employees of one client whose employment this workspace administers — never the company's own staff
  client.hr.recruiting:
    path: 30-CLIENTS/{id}/05-HR/recruiting/
    summary: Candidates and sourcing channels for roles this workspace recruits on one client's behalf
  client.people:

    path: 30-CLIENTS/{id}/50-MARKETING/
    summary: Marketing work for one client — content, campaigns, audits
  client.marketing.youtube:
    path: 30-CLIENTS/{id}/50-MARKETING/05-PRODUCTION/video/youtube/
